question: Should OpenClaw accept a narrow gateway.peers session-tool feature now, or require the broader federation identity/scope contract before adding core cross-gateway messaging?
rationale: The capability is missing, but solving it changes core routing, config, credentials, session-state, and message-delivery behavior across gateway trust boundaries.

options.title: Define federation contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and settle peer identity, operator scopes, delivery guarantees, and session-history semantics before merging implementation work.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow peer PR
options.body: Explicitly accept the gateway.peers direction and require PR #43656 or a replacement to fix conflicts, add upgrade/security proof, and show real multi-gateway behavior.

options.title: Defer to plugin or MCP bridges
options.body: If core federation is out of scope, document supported external bridge patterns and close this only after maintainers decide not to provide a native primitive.

recommendation.title: Define federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and settle peer identity, operator scopes, delivery guarantees, and session-history semantics before merging implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history is strongest on the affected session-tool and gateway-helper files, while broader product/security input is still needed.
